newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland cuts 2-yr, 5-yr fixed bond prices at tender.
newsitem.headline: Poland cuts 2-yr, 5-yr fixed bond prices at tender.

text.p: Poland cut the minimum price of its 16-percent 2-year bond to 92.90 and sold 293 million zlotys worth of bonds after investors bid for 368 million, the treasury said.
It also cut the minimum price of the 12-percent five-year bond to 79.90 and sold 225 million zlotys worth of bonds after investors bid for 369 million.
At the Treasury's joint 700 million zloty tender the average price of the two-year paper, which matures on February 12, 1999, was 93.17.
The average price for the five-year bond, due on February 12, 2002, was 79.92.

At the last two- and five-year bond tender on December 19, 1996, the minimum price of the shorter paper was 93.16 and the average price was 93.26. The previous minimum price for the longer bond was 80.50 and the average was 80.55.
The value date for today's tender is February 5, 1997 for the two-year bond and February 12, 1997 for the five year bond.
